- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% in those periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak observed in 7-day window.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is neutral (0.27–0.53) and price is trending; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture mean-reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–2.5% when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80); apply +0.75% correction to forecast mean.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0) and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 1–2% downward bias to next 5-day forecast.
